# unitconv

A small unit converter for a recipe and logistics app (Java 17, standard library only). The tests are a plain `TestMain` (no
JUnit): `javac -d build $(find . -name '*.java') && java -cp build TestMain`.

## Layout

* `src/unitconv/Converter.java`: the converter.
* `src/unitconv/Unit.java`: a unit (package-private).
* `test/TestMain.java`: tests.

## Basics

Every unit belongs to a dimension (`length`, ...) and is defined by a factor to the base unit of that dimension.

* `new Converter()` knows the length units `m` (the base), `km` (1000 m), `cm` (0.01), `mm` (0.001), `mi` (1609.344),
  `yd` (0.9144), `ft` (0.3048) and `in` (0.0254). Unit names are case-sensitive.
* `converter.convert(value, from, to)` converts a number between two units of the same dimension and returns a `double`
  (`value * factor(from) / factor(to)`). Unknown or `null` unit names, units of different dimensions and values that are
  NaN or infinite are an `IllegalArgumentException`.

## Time units

`s` (base), `ms`, `min`, `h` and `d` in the dimension `time`.

## Mass units

`kg` (base), `g`, `mg`, `lb` and `oz` in the dimension `mass`.

## Time units

`s` (base), `ms`, `min`, `h` and `d` in the dimension `time`.

## Listing units

`units()`, `units(dimension)` (alphabetical copies) and `dimension(unit)`.

## Custom units

`converter.define(name, factor, dimension)` adds a unit (name: 1 to 24 letters, digits or underscores starting with a letter; positive finite factor relative to the base unit; existing dimension; taken names are an `IllegalStateException`).

## Rounded results

`converter.convertRounded(value, from, to, decimals)` rounds half up (away from zero for halves) on the shortest decimal representation; `decimals` 0 to 6.

`converter.parse("12.5 km to mi")` (the word is `to` or `as`, any case) returns the converted number; malformed text is an `IllegalArgumentException` starting with `cannot parse`.

`K` (base), `C` and `F` with offsets (`K = C + 273.15`, `K = (F - 32) * 5 / 9 + 273.15`); values below absolute zero are an `IllegalArgumentException`.

A unit name `a/b` (two simple units) is a ratio with dimension `dim(a)/dim(b)` and factor `factor(a) / factor(b)`; ratios convert into each other when their dimensions match. Offset units are refused.

prompt:
As a recipe app developer, I need rates such as km/h in unitconv. People want to convert rates like kilometres per hour to metres per second.

- A unit name can be a ratio `a/b` of two simple units (exactly one slash, both parts known units, no spaces). Subject: Parsing text requests

Hi,

The converter should understand requests written as text. Could you build this into unitconv?
What we agreed it should do:
 * `converter.parse(text)` converts a request written like `12.5 km to mi` and returns the result as a `double`. * `src/unitconv/Unit.java`: a unit (package-private).
* `test/TestMain.java`: tests.

Every unit belongs to a dimension (`length`, ...) and is defined by a factor to the base unit of that dimension.

* `new Converter()` knows the length units `m` (the base), `km` (1000 m), `cm` (0.01), `mm` (0.001), `mi` (1609.344),
  `yd` (0.9144), `ft` (0.3048) and `in` (0.0254). Unit names are case-sensitive.
* `converter.convert(value, from, to)` converts a number between two units of the same dimension and returns a `double`

`s` (base), `ms`, `min`, `h` and `d` in the dimension `time`.

`units()`, `units(dimension)` (alphabetical copies) and `dimension(unit)`.

`converter.define(name, factor, dimension)` adds a unit (name: 1 to 24 letters, digits or underscores starting with a letter; positive finite factor relative to the base unit; existing dimension; taken names are an `IllegalStateException`).

## Rounded results

`converter.convertRounded(value, from, to, decimals)` rounds half up (away from zero for halves) on the shortest decimal representation; `decimals` 0 to 10.

`converter.parse("12.5 km to mi")` (the word is `to` or `in`, any case) returns the converted number; malformed text is an `IllegalArgumentException` starting with `cannot parse`.

JUnit): `javac -d build $(find . -name '*.java') && java -cp build TestMain`.

## Layout

* `src/unitconv/Converter.java`: the converter.
* `src/unitconv/Unit.java`: a unit (package-private).
* `test/TestMain.java`: tests.

## Basics

Every unit belongs to a dimension (`length`, ...) and is defined by a factor to the base unit of that dimension.

* `new Converter()` knows the length units `m` (the base), `km` (1000 m), `cm` (0.01), `mm` (0.001), `mi` (1609.344),
  `yd` (0.9144), `ft` (0.3048) and `in` (0.0254). Unit names are case-sensitive.
* `converter.convert(value, from, to)` converts a number between two units of the same dimension and returns a `double`
  (`value * factor(from) / factor(to)`). Unknown or `null` unit names, units of different dimensions and values that are
  NaN or infinite are an `IllegalArgumentException`.

## Mass units

`kg` (base), `g`, `mg`, `lb` and `oz` in the dimension `mass`.

## Time units

`s` (base), `ms`, `min`, `h` and `d` in the dimension `time`.

## Listing units

`units()`, `units(dimension)` (alphabetical copies) and `dimension(unit)`.

## Parsing text requests

`converter.parse("12.5 km to mi")` (the word is `to` or `in`, any case) returns the converted number; malformed text is an `IllegalArgumentException` starting with `cannot parse`.

## Rates such as km/h

A unit name `a/b` (two simple units) is a ratio with dimension `dim(a)/dim(b)` and factor `factor(a) / factor(b)`; ratios convert into each other when their dimensions match. Offset units are refused.

UNIT-680  Parsing text requests
Type: Feature | Priority: Low | Component: unitconv

The converter should understand requests written as text.

# Design note: Time units and Rates such as km/h
Status: approved | Owner: Amara

## Time units
Motivation:
People want to convert durations.

Behaviour:
1. The converter also knows the dimension `time`: `s` (the base), `ms` (0.001 s), `min` (60 s), `h` (3600 s) and `d` (86400 s). Mixing time with other dimensions is an `IllegalArgumentException`.

## Rates such as km/h
Motivation:
People want to convert rates like kilometres per hour to metres per second.

Behaviour:
1. A unit name can be a ratio `a/b` of two simple units (exactly one slash, both parts known units, no spaces). The ratio has the dimension `<dimension of a>/<dimension of b>` (`length/time` for `km/h`) and its factor is `factor(a) / factor(b)`, so `36 km/h` is `10 m/s`. Ratios work wherever a unit name is accepted by `convert`; two ratios convert into each other when their dimensions are equal as text (`km/h` and `mi/min` can, `km/h` and `kg/s` cannot, and neither can `km/h` and `m`).
2. Units with an offset cannot be part of a ratio (an `IllegalArgumentException`). Everything else that does not make a valid ratio (`km/`, `/h`, `km/h/s`, unknown parts) is reported as an unknown unit (`IllegalArgumentException`).

## Out of scope
Anything not described above; everything that works today keeps working as it does.
